message.content:
A **paired samples t-test** is used to test whether the **mean difference** between two **related measurements** is significantly different from zero.[1][2][8]

It is appropriate when the same subjects are measured twice, or when observations are matched in pairs, such as **pre-test vs. post-test** scores or left-eye vs. right-eye measurements.[2][3][8]

Key points:

- It works on the **differences within each pair**, then performs a one-sample \(t\)-test on those differences.[1][2][6]
- The main assumptions are:
  - the outcome is **continuous**,
  - the pairs are **related/dependent**,
  - the **differences are approximately normally distributed**,
  - and there are no major outliers in the differences.[3][7][8]
- The test statistic uses the mean difference divided by its standard error, with **\(df = n - 1\)**, where \(n\) is the number of pairs.[2][6][7]

If you want, I can also show:
- the **formula**,
- a **worked example**,
- or how to run it in **R, SPSS, Excel, or Python**.
